documents.title: Pregnant again
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Hi, writing before school. Positive test again, LMP was December 12. Can you send the referral to the same OB group as last time? And do you want the thyroid test again?

Holly

documents.title: RE: Pregnant again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations! Referral sent to the same OB group. Yes, TSH please, same as last time; lab is open 7-11 any weekday. Keep up the prenatal, iron and levothyroxine.

Given what happened after your last delivery, please make sure your OB team has that history front and center. I'll send them a summary with the referral.

documents.title: TSH Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH in range at ~4 wks. No dose change, levothyroxine 75 mcg. Released to portal with note: "Thyroid level looks good. Stay on the same dose."

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Intake Letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Holly Barrett, DOB 07/16/1992
New OB visit 02/06/2024 at 7w6d.

G3P2002. 2017 term vaginal delivery with episiotomy. 06/2023 precipitous term vaginal delivery at home complicated by postpartum hemorrhage from uterine atony requiring uterotonics and transfusion of 2 units.

Hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg, TSH normal per your office in January. Iron deficiency anemia on daily ferrous sulfate. Allergic to penicillin (rash) and latex (contact dermatitis).

Routine prenatal labs within normal limits. Given her history we have counseled her to come in at the first sign of labor and will plan delivery in hospital with active management of the third stage. We will forward results. EDD 09/17/2024.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Levothyroxine Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
eRx renewal request, levothyroxine 0.075 mg, #90. TSH 1/11/24 normal. Pended for PCP, 90 days + 3 RF.
Approved by PCP 3/18.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, identity confirmed.

31F G3P2 at 22w0d, here to keep an eye on iron and thyroid alongside OB care. Prenatal visits going fine per her. Taking ferrous sulfate daily, separate from levothyroxine. No dizziness or fainting. No bleeding.

Exam limited to video: well appearing, conversant, no distress, not pale-looking on camera.

A/P
- Iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy, prior PPH with transfusion: CBC and iron studies this week; continue ferrous sulfate. Want her stores as good as we can get them before delivery. Will share with OB.
- Hypothyroidism: TSH normal in January, continue 75 mcg.
Labs Thursday.

documents.title: CBC and Iron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hgb 11.2, ferritin 13. Similar to last pregnancy at this stage. Continue daily iron. Faxed to OB.

To patient via portal: "Your blood count is holding steady at 11.2. Iron stores are still low, so keep taking the iron every day. I've sent these to your OB."

documents.title: OB Immunization Record
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: OB office faxed vaccine record: Tdap 07/02/2024 at 29 wks. Added to immunization history.

conditions.label: Vaginal laceration causing postpartum hemorrhage
conditions.note: Deep upper vaginal wall laceration, repaired in OR

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Obstetrics Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Holly Barrett, 32 y/o G3 now P3003
Admitted 09/08/2024 02:50. Discharged 09/10/2024.

History: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg; iron deficiency anemia on ferrous sulfate; prenatal vitamin. Postpartum hemorrhage from atony 06/2023 after a home birth, transfused 2 units. Two prior vaginal deliveries.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), latex (contact dermatitis). Latex-free room.

Course: Presented in active labor at 38w5d. Admission Hgb 12.0, Hct 36. Labor progressed over several hours; second stage assisted with forceps. Liveborn male, vigorous. Placenta delivered intact. Active management of the third stage. EBL at delivery 300 mL.

About 30 minutes after delivery she reported ongoing bleeding and felt faint. BP 90/60, HR 110. Fundus firm. Steady vaginal bleeding. Cervix seen and intact on speculum exam; a deep laceration of the upper vaginal wall was identified as the source. Hgb 9.0, Hct 27, platelets 250K, PT 12 s, PTT 30 s.

Taken to the OR; laceration repaired under regional anesthesia with good hemostasis. IV crystalloid given. Not transfused. PPD1 BP 108/66, HR 88, Hgb 8.6. Ambulating, tolerating diet, lochia appropriate.

Discharge diagnoses: term forceps-assisted vaginal delivery; postpartum hemorrhage due to upper vaginal wall laceration, repaired; acute blood loss anemia.
Discharge meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, prenatal vitamin daily.
Follow-up: PCP 1-2 weeks for CBC. OB postpartum visit 6 weeks.

documents.title: Repair of Vaginal Laceration
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OPERATIVE NOTE (received with discharge packet)
Date: 09/08/2024
Preop/postop diagnosis: postpartum hemorrhage, deep upper vaginal wall laceration after forceps-assisted vaginal delivery.
Procedure: exam under anesthesia, repair of vaginal laceration.
Anesthesia: regional.
Findings: uterus firm. Cervix intact circumferentially. Deep laceration of the upper vaginal wall, actively bleeding. No other lacerations.
Description: Patient positioned in lithotomy, latex-free setup. Apex identified and secured. Laceration closed in layers with absorbable suture with hemostasis achieved. Rectal exam normal after repair. Counts correct.
Complications: none further. Condition: stable to recovery.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
TCM call. Delivered 9/8, forceps, PPH from vaginal laceration repaired in OR, not transfused. Home since 9/10.

Pt reports soreness at repair, using ice and sitz baths. Bleeding moderate and decreasing. Mild lightheadedness on standing, no syncope. Baby boy feeding well. Meds reconciled: levothyroxine, ferrous sulfate, prenatal. Reviewed return precautions for heavy bleeding, fever, fainting, foul discharge.

Appt with PCP Mon 9/23 3:30.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-delivery f/u. 2 wks out from forceps delivery 9/8 with PPH from a deep upper vaginal wall laceration, repaired in OR. Hgb 12 -> 9 -> 8.6 PPD1. No transfusion this time.

Feels better than after last delivery. Repair site less sore. Lochia light. Some fatigue, up at night with the baby. No dizziness now. Not back at school yet, on leave until November.
Meds: levothyroxine 75, ferrous sulfate 325 daily, prenatal.

Exam: vitals as charted. NAD. Mild pallor of conjunctivae. RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Calves soft. (Perineal/vaginal exam deferred to OB postpartum visit.)
PHQ-9: 5. Talked through sleep and support; she feels okay, knows to reach out if mood dips.

A/P
1. PPH from vaginal laceration, repaired. Resolved.
2. Acute blood loss anemia on chronic iron deficiency. CBC today. Continue ferrous sulfate daily. CBC + ferritin + TSH in ~10 wks.
3. Hypothyroidism, stable.
TCM done: RN call 9/12, discharge summary and op note reviewed.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 10.3, improving from 8.6. Portal: "Blood count is coming back up, 10.3 now. Keep the iron going. Labs again in early December."

documents.title: Vaccine Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu (trivalent) 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; COVID 2024-25 Moderna 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. 7 wks postpartum. No prior reactions. Latex-free. VIS x2. Observed 15 min without issue.

documents.title: CBC, Iron, TSH
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hgb 11.8, back to her baseline. Ferritin 18. TSH normal on 75 mcg. Blood loss anemia resolved.

Portal: "Hi Holly, your blood count has recovered fully and your thyroid level is normal. Iron stores are still lowish (18), so please keep taking the iron daily. See you for your physical in the spring."

documents.title: Iron question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Two things. I need a refill on the iron. And my mornings are chaos now with a baby and a toddler, so sometimes I end up taking the iron and thyroid pill together. Is that a big deal?

documents.title: RE: Iron question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Refill sent. It does matter a bit: iron can block absorption of levothyroxine. Easiest fix for most people is thyroid pill first thing when you wake up, iron with dinner or at bedtime. If they keep ending up together, let me know and we'll check a TSH sooner. Physical is booked for March 10, we'll check both then.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT
32F, teacher, now mom of three (2017, 6/2023, 9/2024). Back at school since November.

Since last physical: delivery 9/8/24, forceps, PPH from upper vaginal wall laceration repaired in OR; blood loss anemia recovered by December (Hgb 11.8). No other illness.
Thyroid: taking levothyroxine on waking, moved iron to bedtime after our February messages. Feels well.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg at bedtime, prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), latex (contact dermatitis).
FH: mother PPH and T2DM, father HTN. Unchanged.
SH: never smoker. Wine a glass or two a month. Exercise is chasing toddlers.
PHQ-9: 3.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight 67 kg. Well-appearing. Conjunctivae pink. Thyroid smooth, normal size. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT. Ext no edema. Skin no lesions of concern.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: CMP and lipids today given FH. Pap/HPV due 2026. Flu/COVID done in the fall.
2. Hypothyroidism: TSH today.
3. Iron deficiency anemia: CBC, iron studies. Continue ferrous sulfate.
RTC 3 months to recheck iron if ferritin still low, otherwise 1 yr.

documents.title: Physical Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Holly,

Everything from Monday is back. Hemoglobin 12.1, the best I've seen it since you joined us. Ferritin 21, better but still the low end, so keep the iron going. Thyroid normal. Cholesterol, kidney, liver and sugar all normal.

I'd like a quick follow-up in June to recheck iron; the front desk will reach out.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel 3:30 today, end-of-year field day at school and childcare fell through. Offered July dates, she will call back after school lets out.

documents.body: Congratulations, Holly. Referral is in to the same OB group, with a note about both of your prior deliveries. TSH this week, and we'll do CBC and iron around 20 weeks like last time. Keep taking all three pills.

Re: Holly Barrett, DOB 07/16/1992
New OB visit 10/20/2025 at 8w1d. EDD 05/31/2026.

G4P3003. Obstetric history: 2017 vaginal delivery with episiotomy; 06/2023 home delivery with postpartum hemorrhage from atony, transfused; 09/2024 forceps-assisted delivery with postpartum hemorrhage from an upper vaginal wall laceration, repaired in the OR.

Hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg (TSH normal 9/25 per your office). Iron deficiency anemia on ferrous sulfate. Allergies: penicillin, latex.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Levothyroxine Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting levothyroxine 75 mcg #90. Pharmacy says manufacturer changed, pt asked whether that matters. Per PCP ok to fill, same dose; generic levothyroxine from a different manufacturer is fine, she should just stick with it. Sent 90 days + 3 refills.
